Seattle’s climatological August high averages near 77°F, but the persistent marine layer and below-normal 500 mb heights keep values a couple of degrees cooler than peak summer potential. Latest observations show morning temperatures in the mid-60s with dew points supporting limited diurnal range; final resolution hinges on peak readings reported by Sea-Tac or official stations before evening.

The latest JMA three-day guidance issued August 12 at 17:00 lists a maximum of 29°C (minimum 23–24°C) under conditions that limit afternoon insolation, while ensemble models show tight clustering around this value. August climatology sets a normal daily maximum near 31.4°C, but the current pattern—typical of mid-summer instability—introduces downside risk from earlier or heavier showers and limited upside from any unexpected clearing. Updated short-range model runs and the next JMA briefing remain the primary near-term catalysts for any probability shifts before the observation window closes.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts from multiple models cluster Qingdao’s August 13 maximum near 29–31 °C**, producing the tight market distribution around those three outcomes. Qingdao’s coastal setting on the Yellow Sea allows persistent marine air and northeasterly flow to moderate daytime heating, while high humidity (often 70–85 %) and possible late-day cloud build-up or isolated thundershowers further cap the peak.  

Recent model runs show only modest differences in the timing and coverage of any shower activity or afternoon clearing; a slightly earlier or more extensive cloud deck favors 29 °C, while delayed or broken cloud cover supports 30–31 °C. Historical August climatology places the average daily maximum near 29–30 °C, so the current setup sits squarely within the normal envelope rather than an extreme regime.  

Traders are therefore weighting the most probable model consensus and the small but non-zero chance that subtle shifts in boundary-layer moisture or sea-breeze timing push the reading one degree either side of 30 °C.

**Persistent high pressure across southern England, combined with southerly winds drawing hot continental air northward, is sustaining the current heatwave and keeping maximum temperatures elevated into mid-August.** Clear skies and strong solar insolation under this anticyclonic setup favor peak readings in the low-to-mid 30s Celsius for London on August 14, 2026, consistent with Met Office guidance showing daytime highs around 31–34 °C and amber extreme-heat warnings extending through Friday evening. 

Recent model runs indicate the thermal peak occurred on the 13th, with modest cooling or increased boundary-layer mixing expected by the 14th, which narrows the most probable outcomes to 32–33 °C. Ensemble spread and subtle differences in forecast timing of any weak frontal influence or urban heat-island enhancement explain why 33 °C holds a slight edge (32 %) over 32 °C (29.5 %), while 34 °C remains viable but less favored (11.5 %). Longer-range signals of above-average temperatures for the month further support trader consensus around these values rather than cooler or extreme outliers.
